# athenaSim: OB/GYN EHR workspace simulation (fictitious data)

**SIMULATION. Every patient, name, ID, result, note and claim here is fictitious and generated by code.**
A static test environment shaped like an ambulatory OB/GYN EHR workspace: dashboard (inbox counts, weekly
schedule, network panel), full schedule (day per-provider columns, week view), Clinical Inbox with folders,
patient chart (summary, problems, meds, allergies, vitals flowsheet, OB episode / prenatal flowsheet, labs,
imaging, documents/consults, encounters, claims), encounter notes with sign-off, claim worklist (denials with
reason codes and suggested fixes, missing slips, hold), daily practice report, weekly practice dashboard and a recall list.

It is an independent re-creation for automation testing. It contains no vendor code or assets and is not
affiliated with any EHR vendor.

Live: https://storkdoc.github.io/athena-sim/

## Time and data
* Sim date control in the red banner (range 2025-01-01 to 2027-12-31), and the time of day follows your real clock.
  `?simdate=YYYY-MM-DD` starts on a date.
* Deterministic: seed `congressional-sim-v1` produces about 5,200 fictitious patients with pregnancy episodes,
  annual exams and problem visits that are scheduled into provider templates. The same date always gives the same schedule,
  statuses, results, inbox, deliveries and claims. Past days show completed history, while future days show booked visits.
* Your actions (check-in, sign-off, close or route inbox items, bookings, claim fixes) are saved in localStorage.
  **Reset sim** clears them.

## Routes
`#/dashboard`, `#/schedule?d=YYYY-MM-DD&view=day|week`, `#/inbox/<Folder>`, `#/chart/<SIM id>/<tab>`,
`#/encounter/<appt id>`, `#/claims?tab=DENIED|MISSING%20SLIP|HOLD`, `#/report`, `#/dashboard-practice`,
`#/recall`, `#/openslots`, `#/cancellations`, `#/obpatients`, `#/patients?q=`.
`window.SIMDATA` exposes the generator.

## Tests
`node tests/smoke.js` (Playwright Chromium, with `BASE` pointing at a local server) checks every screen for console errors
and exercises the close, check-in, book and date-move flows.

## Patient photos
`photos/` holds 64 AI-generated headshots (160 px WebP, about 2 KB each) of **people who do not exist**. They were made with an
image generator for this simulation and are not photos of any real person. `js/photos.js` gives each patient one photo,
chosen deterministically from the patient ID by sex and age band (age as of 2026-01-01). About 17% of patients get the gray
silhouette and about 6% get an initials tile, as in real charts. Male headshots are used for fictitious partners and
emergency contacts.


## Backfilled clinical record (every patient)

`js/history.js` gives each of the ~5,200 fictitious patients a deterministic multi-year record dated 03/2021-12/2024, before the
scheduled range. That means every patient has a past record on every sim date. The record is built lazily the first time a chart opens, takes about 10-50 ms, and is cached.

- **Patient categories:** *established* (seen here since 2021), *transfer* (new-patient visit in 2023-24 plus faxed outside records from a prior OB/GYN) and *adolescent* (first GYN visit plus pediatric records).
- **Past visits** cover annuals, problem visits that match the problem list, and prenatal and postpartum care. Prenatal care includes prior deliveries in the window and the pre-2025 part of pregnancies that continue into the range. Every visit has a full generated note: reason, HPI, 12-system ROS, 10-system exam, multi-problem A&P, screening, procedures and vitals.
- **Labs** repeat over time from per-patient baselines, so they trend (Hgb, TSH, LDL, A1c, vitamin D, ferritin, CMP) and match the problem list.
- **Imaging** results are full reports: indication, technique, comparison, findings, measurements, impression and a fictitious reader. They include dating, anatomy and growth OB ultrasounds, pelvic US, mammogram, breast US and DXA.
- **Outside documents** have full letter text: MFM, endocrinology, cardiology, breast surgery, GI, behavioral health, pulmonary/sleep, urogynecology, neurology, rheumatology, PCP summary, ED summary, delivery discharge summary and prior-practice records.
- **History slide-out:** medical, surgical, OB (G/P, TPAL, delivery table), GYN, social and family history, plus medication start/stop history and insurance. The **Vaccines** panel lists immunizations. The **Vitals** panel shows all encounters and a prenatal flowsheet for each pregnancy. Portal and phone cases appear under Visits and Cases.
- **Inbox:** backfilled items are already reviewed (closed). Recent in-range results and documents still arrive unreviewed in the Clinical Inbox.

`tests/coverage.js` checks all 5,200 patients on five sim dates (2025-01-02 to 2027-12-30). Each patient must have at least one past visit, lab, imaging report and outside document. On a sample, the test also checks the depth of the notes, reports, documents and history sections, then opens real chart panels.


## Text size and responsive layout

All stylesheet sizes are in `rem` against a fluid root size, `html{font-size:clamp(15px, 12.5px + 0.28vw, 18px)}`. That gives about 15px on phones, 16px on laptops and 18px on 2560 displays, and headings, bars, panels and icons scale with it. Breakpoints:
- **1240px:** the top nav wraps and the dashboard drops to 2 columns.
- **1100px:** the inbox detail pane moves under its list.
- **900px:** tables scroll inside their own container.
- **760px:** the dashboard and chart landing stack, the banner cells wrap, and slide-outs go full width.
- **600px:** the chart rail becomes icons only and the menus wrap.

`tests/responsive.js` checks 17 screens at 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920 and 2560 wide. It fails on any horizontal page overflow, any element outside the viewport that isn't inside its own scroll container, and any console error.

## Ultrasound and MFM reports (js/sono.js, css/sono.css)
Every pregnancy gets ultrasound studies where clinically indicated, dated by gestational age. They are deterministic and fictitious, and each page carries the footer "SIMULATION - fictitious".
- **In-office OB reports** use the Viewpoint-style layout with the letterhead "Congressional OBGYN (SIM)" and run 2 pages:
  - Dating/viability at the NOB visit; a failed-pregnancy scan for SABs.
  - A twin FHR check at 16 weeks.
  - Cervical length at 16/18/22/24 weeks after a prior preterm birth.
  - Anatomy at 19–21 weeks for low-risk patients.
  - Placental follow-up at 28/32 weeks for a low-lying placenta.
  - Growth at 32 weeks for AMA, 32/36 weeks for GDM, 36 weeks for suspected LGA.
  - BPP from 36 weeks for age 40 and over.
- **MFM consult reports** use the letterhead "Chesapeake Perinatal Associates (SIM)" and run 4 pages, including 6 SVG growth charts:
  - NT for AMA, twins, or about 35% of other patients by choice.
  - Detailed anatomy for high-risk patients (AMA, twins, pregestational DM, cHTN, prior PTB).
  - Serial growth and weekly BPP with UA Doppler for twins, pregestational DM, cHTN, gHTN/preeclampsia, and FGR (growth every 2 weeks after onset).
  - Each MFM report is filed under Imaging Results and also as an outside document (History, Clinical Documents inbox).
- Measurements follow each fetus's own z-score trajectory, using Hadlock biometry and EFW. FGR falls below the 10th percentile after onset, LGA rises above the 85th–90th, and twin B tracks below twin A. UA S/D rises with FGR, and uterine artery PI rises with HTN.
- GYN pelvic US results render as a 2-page "Gynecology Report".
- Tests: `tests/sono.js`.
